entries.title: The placeholder Worker class, worker.yaml and optional extras are gone
entries.description: The earlier `Worker` Python class (which only printed a message and ran no jobs), the `acex-worker start` form, the `worker.yaml` example and the `celery` extra no longer exist; Celery is now a normal dependency and the Redis dependency was dropped. The package now depends on the ACEX client and devkit instead of the backend package, and `acex_worker.__version__` is no longer defined.

entries.title: A container image for the worker is built in the dev pipeline
entries.description: A `Dockerfile` for the worker produces an image named `acex-worker` whose entrypoint is `acex-worker`; set `ACEX_BASE_URL`, `ACEX_CLIENT_ID` and `ACEX_CLIENT_SECRET` in the deployment. For now the image is only built and published by the development pipeline, not a release pipeline.

entries.title: Discover vendor CVEs from NVD in background jobs
entries.description:
Workers handle `acex.cve.discover` jobs, fetch paginated NVD results for a vendor
and optional date range, and ingest them through the backend API. Requests use
rate limiting and retries.

The worker fetches the optional NVD API key from the backend once per discovery
job. Without a key, it uses NVD's lower request rate; it does not read
`NVD_API_KEY` from its environment.

entries.title: Job outcomes and redeliveries are handled and reported to the backend
entries.description: A worker claims a job before running it and reports success or failure with a message; a handler error, or a result the backend rejects, shows up as a failed job and in the worker log. A message is acknowledged only after its job has run, so a worker that dies mid-job leaves it to be redelivered, and jobs already finished or cancelled are skipped. Jobs run in threads and the number running in parallel is not configurable by `ACEX_*` settings; scale by running more workers.

entries.title: The worker now runs jobs from the message broker the backend names
entries.description: Start it with the `acex-worker` command. At startup it logs in to the ACEX API, asks the backend which broker and queues carry its job types, and consumes from those queues until stopped. It needs a backend that offers this worker connection endpoint and a reachable broker; if login or the connection request fails, it logs `Worker could not start` and exits with an error.

entries.title: Worker connection is configured with ACEX_* environment variables
entries.description: `ACEX_BASE_URL` is the backend address (defaults to a local development address). `ACEX_CLIENT_ID` and `ACEX_CLIENT_SECRET` are the worker's service-account login; the secret is required when the backend has authentication enabled, otherwise the worker refuses to start instead of opening a browser login. `ACEX_ISSUER_URL` overrides the identity provider the backend reports, and `ACEX_VERIFY_SSL=false` turns off TLS verification.

entries.title: Worker installs and upgrades NED drivers itself from the backend
entries.description: NEDs are not part of the worker image. At startup the worker downloads every NED the backend publishes that is missing or at another version and pip-installs it, so it needs access to a package index for their dependencies. If a NED is upgraded after it was already loaded, the worker shuts down gracefully (running jobs finish) and the job fails, so run workers under something that restarts them.

entries.title: Workers can discover a device that has just fetched its ZTP bootstrap
entries.description: The new job type `acex.ztp.discover` logs in to the device with the bootstrap login set on its ZTP method, using the NED chosen for that method, and reports serial number, vendor, hardware model, OS and OS version. The job fails with a clear message if the method has no NED chosen or no bootstrap username and password.

entries.title: Workers can provision a node's configuration over ZTP
entries.description: The new job type `acex.ztp.provision` sends the node's logical-node configuration to the device through its primary management connection, using the NED of the node's asset and the method's bootstrap login, then sets the node's provision status to provisioned. The job fails if the node has no primary management connection with an IP address.

entries.title: Workers render and apply configuration patches
entries.description: Workers handle `acex.operations.patch.render` and `acex.operations.patch.apply`. Every configuration they read from a node is uploaded as its observed configuration.

entries.title: Workers run commands and pings on nodes
entries.description: Workers take `acex.operations.execute` and `acex.operations.actions.ping` jobs from the new `acex.operations` queue. They log in with the node's assigned credentials over its management connection. Command output is masked by the node's driver before it is reported; ping reports packets sent and received, round-trip times and success rate. Restart workers to pick up the new queue.

entries.title: Workers run the steps of workflow runs
entries.description:
Workers take `acex.operations.workflow.*` jobs from the `acex.operations` queue:

- Execute and action steps render their templates for each node from earlier artifacts, then run like the bulk
  operations.
- Probe steps ping from the worker itself, without privileges. This needs `icmplib`, a new dependency of the
  worker.
- Compute, assert and condition steps read earlier artifacts without logging in anywhere.

Every step computes the artifacts it names over its own result. In a dry run no device is reached. Restart
workers so they register the new job types.

entries.title: A failed job's error is the reason, without the handler's name
entries.description:
Before, a job's error read like `Handler HandleExecute for job 212 (acex.operations.execute) raised '...'`. Now it
is just the reason, for example `Node 4 has no primary management connection with an IP`. An unexpected error
keeps its type in front, for example `KeyError: 'x'`. Which handler raised it, and where, is still in the
worker's log.
